title: Jharkhand Exam Scam: CID Arrests Key Accused's Wife and Brother as Probe Widens
excerpt: The ₹40 crore exam fraud racket has toppled JPSC leadership, triggered an ED money laundering probe, and left nine recruitment processes suspended across the state.
body:
• CID arrested the wife and brother of Abhay Tiwari, the alleged mastermind of a ₹40 crore exam fraud racket in Jharkhand, following raids across six districts.
  • Tiwari, a state government staffer who cleared 12 competitive exams in 13 years, was arrested earlier as the central figure in paper leaks affecting JSSC-CGL, Civil Services, and other major exams.
  • All three JPSC members have resigned amid the widening scandal, while the Enforcement Directorate has launched a money laundering probe under PMLA.
  • Students have been protesting for over 16 days demanding a CBI investigation, as nine major recruitment processes remain suspended statewide.

Jharkhand's Criminal Investigation Department has arrested the wife and brother of Abhay Tiwari, the alleged mastermind behind a ₹40 crore examination fraud racket that has upended the state's recruitment system and triggered a political crisis.

The arrests came after CID conducted simultaneous raids at 18 locations across Ranchi, Palamu, Hazaribagh, Bokaro, and Dhanbad. More than 14 people had already been arrested before Tiwari himself was taken into custody, and the net continues to widen.

How the Racket Worked

Tiwari, a Jharkhand state government employee, drew investigators' attention after records showed he had cleared 12 competitive examinations in just 13 years — an extraordinary pattern that pointed to systemic fraud rather than individual brilliance.

https://x.com/WIONews/status/2089773483597475953

According to investigators, Tiwari ran a sophisticated operation that compromised question papers for multiple high-stakes examinations, including the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission's Combined Graduate Level (JSSC-CGL) exam, JPSC Civil Services, Excise Constable recruitment, and even the Class 10 Board examination and NEET-UG.

"The accused built a network spanning multiple districts, involving government insiders and middlemen who facilitated paper leaks for cash."

— CID investigators, per media reports

Institutional Fallout

The scandal has gutted the Jharkhand Public Service Commission. All three sitting JPSC members — Ajeeta Bhattacharya, the wife of a JMM leader, along with Anima Hansda and Jamal Ahmad — have resigned. Former JPSC chairperson L. Khiangte has been arrested.

The Enforcement Directorate has opened a Prevention of Money Laundering Act investigation into the financial trail behind the racket, signaling that the probe is expanding beyond exam fraud into organized financial crime.

Nine major recruitment processes across the state have been suspended as authorities work to determine which results may have been compromised. The JPSC has already postponed its Civil Services Mains examination indefinitely.

Student Protests Intensify

Thousands of students have been protesting across Jharkhand for more than 16 days, demanding a Central Bureau of Investigation probe rather than relying on the state-run CID. Protesters argue that the scale of the racket — spanning multiple agencies and exam cycles — exceeds what a state body can credibly investigate.

"Our futures have been stolen. We prepared for years while connected people bought their way through."

— Student protester, Ranchi

The protests echo broader frustrations across India with examination integrity. Paper leaks have hit states from Rajasthan to Bihar in recent years, and the NEET-UG scandal in 2024 led to nationwide outrage and Supreme Court intervention.

What's Next

The CID has indicated that more arrests are likely as investigators trace the financial network behind the racket. The ED's PMLA investigation could uncover the full scale of money changing hands across exam cycles.

For the thousands of candidates whose results now hang in uncertainty, the immediate question is whether suspended exams will be re-conducted and when — a timeline no authority has yet committed to. The demand for a CBI takeover continues to grow louder.
nri_angle: The exam fraud crisis underscores systemic integrity challenges in Indian competitive examinations that affect diaspora families whose relatives sit for state-level recruitment tests.
